title: Multiply & divide fractions
examples: When I see 'of' in a word problem, do I multiply?
Can you show me another example of keep change flip?
What is the easiest way to remember keep change flip?

explain.say: Today we will learn to multiply and divide fractions. Remember that 'of' in a word problem means we should multiply.
To multiply fractions, you multiply the top numbers together. Then you multiply the bottom numbers together. Keep the top numbers and keep the bottom numbers.
For example, three fourths times one half equals three halves over four. So we multiply three by one, and four by two. The answer is three sixths over eight.
Dividing fractions uses a trick called keep change flip. You keep the first fraction, change the division sign to multiplication, and flip the second fraction. This is very important.

Let us try six divided by three fourths. We keep six over one, change to multiply, and flip three fourths to four thirds. So we multiply six over one by four over three. The answer is twenty four thirds over three.

faq.q: Does 'of' always mean multiply when I see it?
faq.a: Yes, in math problems, the word 'of' usually means multiplication. You should multiply the two numbers given.
asks: If I see 'of', should I multiply?

faq.q: What does 'keep change flip' mean for division?
faq.a: It means you keep the first fraction as it is. You change the division sign to a multiplication sign. Then you flip the second fraction upside down.
asks: How do I use keep change flip?
What is the rule for dividing fractions?

faq.q: Can I simplify my answer after multiplying fractions?
faq.a: Yes, it is always best to simplify your final answer. You can divide the top and bottom numbers by the same number. This makes the fraction smaller.
asks: Is it okay to leave big numbers?

faq.q: What if I multiply a whole number by a fraction?
faq.a: You can write the whole number as a fraction over one. For example, five is five over one. Then you multiply five over one by the fraction.
asks: Do I need to change whole numbers?

faq.q: Why do I have to flip the second fraction when dividing?
faq.a: Flipping the second fraction is the rule for dividing fractions. It changes the division problem into an easier multiplication problem.
asks: Why do we flip the second number?
Is there a reason for flipping?

facts: To multiply fractions, multiply the numerators together and the denominators together.
When dividing fractions, you keep the first fraction, change the sign, and flip the second fraction.
A whole number can be written as that number over one.
The process of keeping, changing, and flipping is key for division.

quiz.say: Calculate three fifths multiplied by two fifths.
quiz.why: You multiply the top numbers three times two, which is six. You multiply the bottom numbers five times five, which is twenty five. So the answer is six twenty five.

wrong.1: This mistake happens when you add the denominators instead of multiplying them.
wrong.2: This mistake happens when you divide the numerators instead of multiplying them.
wrong.3: This mistake happens when you only multiply the top and bottom numbers separately.

quiz.say: What is one and one half divided by one third?
quiz.why: First, change one and one half to three halves. Then, keep three halves, change to multiply, and flip one third to three ones. So we multiply three over two by three over one. The answer is nine over two.

wrong.1: This mistake happens if you multiply the numerators and denominators separately.
wrong.2: This mistake happens if you only multiply the first fraction by the numerator of the second.
wrong.3: This mistake happens if you forget to flip the second fraction.

quiz.say: How many three fourths are in two?
quiz.why: We write two as two over one. Then we keep two over one, change to multiply, and flip three fourths to four three. We multiply two by four, and one by three. The answer is eight over three.

wrong.0: This mistake happens if you only divide the whole number by the numerator.
wrong.1: This mistake happens if you treat it like a multiplication problem.
wrong.3: This mistake happens if you multiply the numerators and denominators incorrectly.
